mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of rising housing starts than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months, it indicates strong real demand growth, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when real consumption growth outpaces inflation than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong payroll growth than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising faster than 2% annually, it indicates a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in high inflation and tight monetary policy periods than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month, it indicates strong economic growth and demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% QoQ and HOUST growth > 5% MoM
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong GDP and housing growth than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
